newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB sees no change in Singapore rates.
newsitem.headline: UOB sees no change in Singapore rates.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd said on Thursday it did not expect a change in Singapore's prime lending rate this year.
UOB chairman and chief executive officer Wee Cho Yaw told reporters the Singapore money market was still very liquid and there was no clear reason to raise rates.
He said the situation in the United States, where interest rates were raised by 0.25 of a percentage point earlier this week, was different.
"There's still a concern there about inflation. Perhaps this year they may have another increase of 0.25 percent," he said.
"But I don't think Singapore prime rates will increase because in Singapore interbank rates are still between three and 3.5 percent. It is unlikely Singapore prime rates will be increased," he said.
